article.title: UAW President Shawn Fain, International Executive Board Sworn In for New Four-Year Term
article.author: Justin Mayhugh
article.content: United Auto Workers (UAW) President Shawn Fain and the union’s newly elected International Executive Board (IEB) were sworn into office for a new four-year term in a ceremony honoring the will of the membership and reaffirming the union’s commitment to fighting for its members and all working-class people. Press is encouraged to use photos from the swearing-in ceremony . The ceremony marked the beginning of a new term for Fain and the International Executive Board, who pledged to faithfully serve the union’s membership and advance the interests of UAW members, families, and their communities. UAW member and longtime union leader Paul Caucci administered the oath of office to Fain, who begins his second term as International Union president. Fain then administered the constitutional obligation to the newly elected members of the International Executive Board. In remarks following the ceremony, Fain reflected on the responsibility of union leadership and outlined the priorities for the next four years: growing the UAW, building worker power and winning improvements for working-class people. Fain connected the UAW’s history of collective action to the challenges facing workers today, pointing to the legacy of the 1930s sit-down strikes and the union’s more recent Stand Up Strike in 2023. “Our union built the American Dream,” Fain said. “From the Sit Down Strikers of the 1930’s to the Stand-Up Strikers since 2023, regular working-class people have led this union and led this country from the ground up.” “Over the next four years, our job is to do more than just to ensure the survival of our organization,” Fain said. “We need to grow. We need to build. We need to win. And to do that, we need each other.” Fain emphasized that the UAW is a democratic, member-driven organization and that the union’s future depends on members being prepared and empowered to fight for their interests. “This is a democracy,” Fain said. “We are only in this room because the members put us in this room. And we will only win what the members are prepared and empowered to fight for.” The president also highlighted the broader stakes of the labor movement, citing wealth inequality and the influence of corporate power as challenges facing working people. He urged UAW leaders to meet those challenges through faith, solidarity and collective action. “The only path to turning this situation around is by abandoning fear and having faith that’s rooted in solidarity,” Fain said. Fain closed his remarks by calling on the board to approach the next four years with a shared sense of purpose and responsibility. “It’s not our individual legacies on the line. It’s not just our union on the line,” Fain said. “It’s the fate of the working class and the fate of humanity.” “And together, we will rise to the occasion—to meet our generation’s defining moment. And we will do it as a United UAW.” Newly Sworn-In UAW International Executive Board The International Executive Board members sworn into office alongside President Fain are: President: Shawn Fain Secretary-Treasurer: Brandon Campbell Vice President: Laura Dickerson Vice President: Kevin Gotinsky Vice President: Ryan Hiestand Region 1 Director: LaShawn English Region 1A Director: Mark DePaoli Region 1D Director: Scott Zuckschwerdt Region 2B Director: David Green Region 4 Director: Lucas DeSpain Region 6 Director: Mike Miller Region 8 Director: Tim Smith Region 9 Director: Jimmy Lakeman Region 9A Director: Brandon Mancilla The UAW enters its new term focused on expanding the union’s reach through a $100 million investment in new organizing, building worker power and fighting for a better future for workers and their families. As growing wealth inequality threatens the foundations of democracy, the union will confront the challenges and opportunities posed by artificial intelligence and automation, fight for a new trade policy that puts workers first, and fight for a political system that puts workers at the center. The focus of this work will remain the UAW’s core priorities: higher wages, quality health care, retirement security and more time off the job.
